structure.unit: Uniform Fiduciary Income And Principal Act

law.catch_line: Transfer from income to principal for depreciation

text.section: As used in this section, "depreciation" means a reduction in value due to wear, tear, decay, corrosion, or gradual obsolescence of a tangible asset having a useful life of more than one year.

A fiduciary may transfer to principal a reasonable amount of the net cash receipts from a principal asset that is subject to depreciation, but may not transfer any amount for depreciation:
Of the part of real property used or available for use by a beneficiary as a residence;
Of tangible personal property held or made available for the personal use or enjoyment of a beneficiary; or
Under this section, to the extent the fiduciary accounts: a. Under § 64.2-1057 for the asset; or b. Under § 64.2-1050 for the business or other activity in which the asset is used.
An amount transferred to principal under this section need not be separately held.
